Tokens & specs

Use the table's menu to select a token set. The search bar set only contains tokens for the unfocused search bar. The search view set contains all other tokens when interacting with search, including all styles and layouts. Learn more about design tokens
Anatomy

Search includes a search bar and a container for suggestions and results. The container is empty by default. Use the list component to add content. In the divided (baseline) style, a divider separates the search bar and results.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Usage

Search helps people find information quickly.

Use search for products with many items to manage, such as files or messages.

contentChunks.footer: Search helps people find information in large inboxes like messages or emails
contentChunks.altText: Mobile UI shows a search bar at the top of a message inbox.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Different ways to search

The search entry point is dependent on a product’s needs, and should be easy to find:

  • Search bar: Use to search contents in a specific view, like Search your messages

  • Search app bar: Use this app bar variant when search is the primary, global function

  • Search icon button: Use when search is a secondary action or not the main focus

contentChunks.footer: Add a search bar below a title to search specific content
contentChunks.altText: A mobile app with a search bar below the page title.

contentChunks.footer: For global search, use a persistent search app bar, integrated into an app bar
contentChunks.altText: A mobile app with a search app bar.

contentChunks.footer: Use a search icon button when search is a secondary action
contentChunks.altText: A mobile app with a magnifying glass icon on the leading side of the app bar.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Focused search

When a search entry point is selected, it opens focused search.  

  • Search suggestions can appear before text is entered

  • Search results can show as someone is typing or after a search is executed

  • Individual elements maintain their own interaction states when search is focused

More on search states

contentChunks.footer: When focused, a search bar expands to show search suggestions or results in a list
contentChunks.altText: Focused search with a list of suggestions on a mobile screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue: If search is the primary action, focused search can be a standalone destination reached from a navigation bar.

contentChunks.footer: Focused search can be a standalone destination, reached by selecting an item in a navigation bar
contentChunks.altText: Focused search on a mobile screen with a list of suggested contacts.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Search suggestions & results

Search suggestions and results both appear in a list component by default.

To help people find information quickly, consider adding variety and context, such as:

  • Leading icons related to suggestions

  • Category labels, like Recent, Contacts, or Suggestions

  • Avatars or other high-priority items

  • Filter chips to narrow down results

contentChunks.footer: Include high-priority items like avatars in search suggestions or results
contentChunks.altText: Search with suggestions organized in a column, ending with a row of 5 contact avatars with names.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Gaps

Use gaps to separate a list of suggestions or results into groups.

More on using gaps in lists

contentChunks.footer: To separate list items into distinct groups, use a gap
contentChunks.altText: A gap separates the location and calendar list items from people and pets avatars.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Placement
A search bar is typically placed at the top of a screen to remain prominent and accessible. Its location depends on whether search is the primary focus of a product or a secondary action.

contentChunks.footer: A search bar can be the primary focus of a page
contentChunks.altText: Mobile UI with a search bar directly below a Settings headline.

contentChunks.footer: Search bars should usually be placed at the top of the content
contentChunks.altText: Mobile UI with a search bar centered at the top of the screen, above a row of Favorites avatars.

contentChunks.footer: Search can be a secondary action
contentChunks.altText: A photos app with a search icon.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Focused search layouts

When focused, search suggestions and results appear in a list below the search bar.  

There are two layout options:

  • Docked opens a list below the search bar, with a scrim covering main content

  • Full-screen expands to fill the screen

More on adaptive design

contentChunks.altText: Tablet UI shows a list of search results docked below the search bar.

contentChunks.footer: Full-screen layout on mobile
contentChunks.altText: Mobile UI shows a list of search results filling the screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Anatomy

contentChunks.footer:
1. Search bar container

  2. Leading icon

  3. Supporting text

  4. Avatar or trailing icon (optional)

  5. Input text

  6. Container for search suggestions or results
contentChunks.altText: 6 elements of search.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Search bar container

In the contained style, the search bar container remains the same shape in both the unfocused and focused states. Avoid changing the container behavior.

The container’s margins should be:

  • Unfocused: 24dp

  • Focused: 12dp

In the divided (baseline) style, a divider separates the search bar and results.

contentChunks.footer: Search bar containers have persistent, rounded corners
contentChunks.altText: Side-by-side comparison of a search container in unfocused and focused states.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Container color

Search bars use the surface container high color role. This role applies when the screen background is white or a tonal surface color, ensuring the container has clear contrast.

contentChunks.footer: Search bars use surface container high to provide clear contrast
contentChunks.altText: 2 mobile UIs show search bars on white and tonal backgrounds.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Avoid using a surface container high color on a surface container background. This can cause the search bar to blend in, making it difficult for people to find.

To ensure proper contrast, use surface container roles that are more than one step apart.

contentChunks.footer: Using a surface container high color on a surface container background reduces contrast and may affect accessibility
contentChunks.altText: A “surface container high” search bar on a “surface container” background.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Icons & icon buttons

Leading icons

The leading side of a search bar should include either:

  • A navigational icon button, such as a menu or arrow

  • A non-functional search icon

contentChunks.footer: A search bar can contain a non-functional search icon
contentChunks.altText: A search bar on a tablet screen contains a non-functional search icon and a trailing avatar.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Trailing icons

A search bar should have one or two trailing icons or icon buttons.

Trailing actions can include:

  • Additional modes of searching like voice search

  • A separate high-level action such as current location or profile

  • An overflow menu

  • A decorative search icon

contentChunks.footer: Use a maximum of two trailing icons
contentChunks.altText: A search bar with 2 trailing icon buttons: a microphone and an overflow menu.

contentChunks.footer: Combine an avatar with up to one other trailing icon button
contentChunks.altText: A search bar with a trailing microphone icon and avatar.

contentChunks.footer: Focused search can show an optional clear icon to remove input text
contentChunks.altText: Focused search with a trailing x icon to clear input text.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Text

Hinted search text

Provide a short description of the information people can search, like Search replies or Search your messages.

Input text

When a person starts typing, the hinted text is replaced with the input text.

contentChunks.footer: Hinted search text is replaced when a search query is entered
contentChunks.altText: A search bar labeled “Search replies”. “Peanut is entered and “Quick results” appear.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Adaptive design

The search bar position and alignment should scale with the layout, and stay close to the searchable content.

In most cases, a search bar should:

  • Stay in its pane and scale in width accordingly

  • Internal elements anchor to the left and right as the parent container scales

More on applying layout

contentChunks.footer: Keep the search bar close to the content a person can search
contentChunks.altText: A search bar keeps its layout region and scales with different window sizes and layouts.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Focused search

When focused, search can switch between showing suggestions or results in a:

  • Docked layout: Best for medium and expanded windows

  • Full-screen layout: Default for compact breakpoints

More on search layouts

contentChunks.footer:
1. A docked layout on a large screen

  2. A full-screen layout, the default for compact screens
contentChunks.altText: Search suggestions in docked and full screen layouts.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Search suggestions or results should swap from full-screen in compact windows to docked in larger breakpoints.

contentChunks.footer: Search suggestions and results should adapt to fit different window sizes
contentChunks.altText: Animation shows search suggestions adapting from full-screen on mobile to a docked layout as the window size increases.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Behavior
Focused search

When a search bar is selected, search becomes focused and can:

  • Show historical suggestions before typing

  • Show suggestions or results as someone is typing

  • Wait to show suggestions or results until a search is queried 

The back icon releases focus, dismisses any suggestions or results, and returns the search bar to its original state.

contentChunks.footer: When focused, a list of search suggestions can appear
contentChunks.altText: When a search bar is tapped, it becomes focused, and suggestions appear in a list.

contentChunks.footer: Focus is released when the back icon is selected
contentChunks.altText: A person searches a photo app. The back icon returns the search bar to its original state.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Scroll

Depending on needs, a search bar can:

  • Scroll away with content, then reappear when a person begins scrolling up

  • Remain fixed at the top of the screen

contentChunks.footer: A search bar can scroll up with content, then reappear when a person scrolls down
contentChunks.altText: Scrolling up hides the search bar. It reappears when scrolling down.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Search results

To execute a search, a person can:

  • Type a query and press Enter

  • Select a suggestion or result without querying a search

Search results appear in a list below the bar, and scroll beneath the bar.   

For accessibility, focused search needs a clear status indicator that it’s searching content, like a search icon or Results label. More on search accessibility

contentChunks.footer: Show search results in a compact, organized list, with an indicator like Quick results
contentChunks.altText: “Peanut” is the entered search query and the first suggestion in the list.

contentChunks.htmlValue: When search results are queried, the input text should remain visible, but not in focus.

contentChunks.footer: Search suggestions and results display in a list, and the input text remains visible
contentChunks.altText: “Pla” is entered into the search bar, “Plants” is suggested and selected.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Predictive back

On Android, predictive back allows a person to swipe left or right on search. 

  • Search detaches from the screen edge to signal the full-screen layout will minimize

  • The previous screen is revealed in a preview

More predictive back design guidance

contentChunks.footer: The search surface and content scale back in the direction of the gesture
contentChunks.altText: Swiping left on search causes the Android screen to scale left.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Use cases

People should be able to use assistive technology to:

  • Navigate to and focus on a search bar

  • View the hinted search text or persistent label

  • Input text and complete a search

  • Interact with a list of search suggestions and results

  • Clear the input text
Interaction & style

Autosuggest

When search suggestions and results appear, the screen reader must announce the change. This lets people know list items are available for selection.

contentChunks.footer: Autocomplete results should be announced by the screen reader
contentChunks.altText: Hinted search text and autocomplete results on a mobile screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Initial focus
Initial focus lands on the first interactive element. This is often a leading icon button or text field. A leading icon button usually activates search directly or opens a navigation component.

contentChunks.footer: Initial focus can land on a leading icon
contentChunks.altText: Search bar with a focused leading icon.

contentChunks.footer: If there’s no leading icon, focus lands on the text field
contentChunks.altText: Search bar with no leading icon. The text field is focused.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Keyboard navigation

Keys

Actions

Tab or Shift + Tab

Navigate between interactive elements

Space or Enter

Activate the search text field for input

Arrows

Navigate between search result items
Labeling elements

The hinted search text should be used as the accessibility label describing the search bar.  

The role for the input field should be:

  • Android: Text field

  • iOS: Search field

contentChunks.footer: The accessibility label should match the hinted search text
contentChunks.altText: Search bar with “Label: Search messages” and “Role: Text field”.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Leading and trailing icon buttons should be labeled according to their accessibility guidance.

contentChunks.footer: Use icon labels for icon buttons
contentChunks.altText: A search bar with accessibility labels for its leading icon button and trailing avatar.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Search suggestions and results use the list component. Screen readers automatically announce the results as a list.

For accessibility labels, follow the list accessibility guidelines.

contentChunks.footer: Search suggestions and results are created using lists
contentChunks.altText: A search bar on mobile, showing search results in a list.
